detail.abstract:
The rapid growth of the digital economy has fundamentally transformed global business operations, prompting significant reconsideration of traditional transfer pricing mechanisms. As multinational corporations (MNCs) increasingly engage in digital business models such as e-commerce platforms, cloud services, and digital marketplaces, the allocation of profits across jurisdictions has become more complex, raising challenges for compliance with existing tax frameworks (OECD, 2022). This study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining a comprehensive literature review, case study analysis of leading digital MNCs, and assessment of financial data to evaluate the interplay between digitalization and transfer pricing adjustments (Kleinbard, 2021; Avi-Yonah, 2020). 
Findings reveal that digital business models often distort traditional cost-plus and transactional net margin methods, creating opportunities for both efficiency gains and potential tax base erosion (Picciotto, 2021). Moreover, regulatory frameworks lag behind technological advancements, increasing the risk of inconsistent tax compliance across jurisdictions (Brauner, 2022). The study highlights critical policy implications, emphasizing the need for updated guidance that balances revenue optimization with fair taxation of digital profits. By elucidating these dynamics, the research provides actionable insights for policymakers seeking to modernize transfer pricing regulations and for MNCs aiming to navigate digital-era tax planning responsibly (OECD, 2022). Ultimately, understanding the interaction between digital economy growth and transfer pricing adjustments is essential for sustaining equitable international tax systems and supporting strategic corporate decision-making.

title: Internal Control Effectiveness in Public Financial Management Systems

detail.title: Internal Control Effectiveness in Public Financial Management Systems
detail.abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of internal control systems in public financial management (PFM) and their influence on transparency, accountability, and operational efficiency. Drawing on recent literature (Ekiru et al., 2024; Masanja & Masimba, 2024), the research adopts a mixed-method approach, combining case studies, surveys, and secondary data analysis from selected public institutions (Otoo et al., 2023; Jarah et al., 2023). Findings indicate that robust internal control mechanisms are strongly associated with improved regulatory compliance, reduced incidences of financial mismanagement, and enhanced organizational performance (ARBOGAST, 2023; Napitupulu, 2023). Specifically, institutions with well-designed control frameworks demonstrate greater transparency in reporting, higher accountability among staff, and more efficient resource utilization. The study further identifies that internal control effectiveness can be strengthened through targeted staff training, strategic adoption of information technology, and comprehensive policy reforms (Purba et al., 2023; Audit trails, 2023). These insights highlight the pivotal role of internal controls in promoting sustainable PFM practices, ensuring that public resources are managed responsibly, and supporting the broader goals of good governance. By emphasizing both technical and organizational dimensions, the study contributes practical recommendations for policymakers and financial managers seeking to enhance institutional performance.

title: Public Sector Corruption and its Effect on Revenue Collection

detail.title: Public Sector Corruption and its Effect on Revenue Collection
detail.abstract: Public sector corruption remains a pervasive challenge, significantly eroding government revenue and compromising the efficiency of public financial management (Sadik-Zada et al., 2024; Bogetić & Naeher, 2024). This study critically examines the mechanisms through which corruption affects revenue collection by conducting a comprehensive review of existing literature, analyzing illustrative case studies, and synthesizing empirical data from multiple jurisdictions. Findings indicate that corruption directly diminishes tax compliance, weakens administrative efficiency in revenue collection, and undermines public trust in government institutions (Jaafar & Muhammad, 2024; Galiński, 2024). The evidence further highlights that both petty and grand corruption distort fiscal policies, creating incentives for tax evasion and inefficiencies in the allocation of public resources. By elucidating these dynamics, the study underscores the importance of targeted anti-corruption strategies and digital governance reforms. Implementing such interventions can enhance transparency, strengthen compliance, and ultimately improve government revenue mobilization. The insights from this synthesis offer practical guidance for policymakers seeking to mitigate the detrimental effects of corruption and foster more accountable, resilient, and efficient public financial management systems (Rahman et al., 2024; Olabanji et al., 2024).

title: Role of Financial Reporting in Enhancing Accountability

detail.title: Role of Financial Reporting in Enhancing Accountability
detail.abstract:
Financial reporting plays a pivotal role in ensuring accountability within both public and corporate organizations (Dimitrov, 2024). This study investigates the relationship between financial reporting practices and organizational accountability, emphasizing transparency, accuracy, and timeliness. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the research combines a comprehensive literature review, case analysis of selected public and corporate entities, and statistical evaluation of reporting practices and their outcomes. The analysis reveals that transparent financial reporting significantly enhances accountability by providing stakeholders with reliable information for decision-making, enabling effective oversight, and reducing opportunities for financial mismanagement (Efunniyi et al., 2024; Berliana et al., 2024). 
Case studies demonstrate that organizations with robust reporting frameworks exhibit higher levels of stakeholder trust, operational efficiency, and compliance with regulatory standards. Statistical findings further corroborate the positive correlation between reporting transparency and reduced incidences of financial irregularities. The study concludes that accurate, transparent, and timely financial reporting is not merely a compliance requirement but a critical instrument for fostering organizational integrity, promoting responsible governance, and mitigating risks associated with mismanagement (Kheriollahi & Ghorbani, 2023). These findings underscore the need for organizations to adopt and maintain rigorous reporting standards, implement effective monitoring mechanisms, and continuously enhance transparency practices to strengthen accountability. Future research is recommended to explore the role of emerging technologies, such as digital reporting platforms and artificial intelligence, in further enhancing the effectiveness of financial reporting systems.

title: Principles Of Legitimate Expectations And Legal Certainty In The Context Of Amendments To Eu Law And National Legislation

detail.title: Principles Of Legitimate Expectations And Legal Certainty In The Context Of Amendments To Eu Law And National Legislation
detail.abstract: The paper concerns selected problems related to the complex topic of changes to the EU law and national legislation. It deals with the so-called prior effectiveness of the EU directives and the retroactivity of (ordinary) laws adopted by the EU member states. The research perspective focuses on the functioning of these institutions vis-à-vis the principles of legitimate expectations and legal certainty. The article is primarily based on the analytical method, as well as the empirical method, drawing on the extensive case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union and the Supreme Administrative Court in Poland. Based on the research carried out by the author, it must be concluded, firstly, that an EU directive during its transposition period in an EU member state cannot be a source of legitimate expectations of an individual. Secondly, the principle of legal certainty is not negated when a normative act receives retroactive effect by way of an exception in order to protect the public interest, provided that legitimate expectations of individuals are guaranteed.

title: Structural Market Modeling vs Heuristic Trading Concepts A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis of the BLT Theory

detail.title: Structural Market Modeling vs Heuristic Trading Concepts A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis of the BLT Theory
detail.abstract:
The proliferation of liquidity-based trading concepts such as Inner Circle Trader
(ICT) methodologies and Smart Money Concepts (SMC) has introduced significant
ambiguity into modern trading discourse, where heuristic execution frameworks are
often conflated with formal market theories. This paper presents a comparative
analysis distinguishing the Boutgajouft Liquidity Triangle Theory  (BLT theory) from both

heuristic trading methodologies and classical technical analysis frameworks.

The analysis demonstrates that BLT Theory constitutes a formal structural market
model characterized by deterministic geometric constructs, empirically testable
predictions, regime-invariant structural properties, and implementation independence
from discretionary trader interpretation.

A multi-dimensional comparative framework is employed to examine theoretical
construction, formal definition, empirical validation, and algorithmic suitability.
The results indicate that BLT Theory occupies a fundamentally distinct epistemological
category from heuristic frameworks such as ICT/SMC, classical technical indicators,
and statistical pattern recognition systems.

Empirical validation across multiple asset classes and extended historical periods
supports the presence of stable structural properties consistent with the theoretical
framework. The contribution of this work lies in clarifying conceptual boundaries
between descriptive trading heuristics and formal structural market theories, thereby
supporting more rigorous academic research and systematic trading development.

detail.title: Rethinking Public Law 86-272 in the Digital Economy
detail.abstract:
This article examines how PL 86-272 operates in the context of modern digital commerce. Rather than

advancing legal conclusions or policy prescriptions, the analysis focuses on functional activity—how digital

systems operate, how customers interact with sellers throughout the sales lifecycle, and why traditional

solicitation concepts have become increasingly difficult to apply. Particular attention is given to website

functionality, cookies and analytics, third-party fulfillment, multistate guidance, and New York’s application of

the statute under Article 9-A. The goal is to provide practitioners with a clearer framework for evaluating PL

86-272 in a commercial environment that no longer aligns with its original design.

title: Donor Standing To Enforce Charitable Gifts In The 21st Century

detail.title: Donor Standing To Enforce Charitable Gifts In The 21st Century

keywords: Uniform Prudent Management of Institutional Funds Act

detail.abstract: This Article outlines the current state of the law regarding donor standing, which illustrates two realities. First, there is an increasing lack of coherence in the law, which has negative consequences, including that the same charitable gift may now be subject to different donor-standing rules depending on completely arbitrary factors. Second, the trend is in favor of granting donors and certain others standing, although this trend is occurring in a haphazard way. This Article also discusses the various factors that led the law of donor standing down this path. Among other things, there has been a gradual normalization of the concept of donor standing since the turn of the century. In addition, there are various factors that support donor standing, which courts have increasingly recognized, including the well-known deficiencies in attorney general oversight, the reality that charities sometimes behave badly, and the fact that in states that allow donor standing, whether by statute or judicial decision, there has not been a flood of vexatious lawsuits filed against charities. This Article briefly concludes by explaining that the law governing charitable gifts has been fragmented in many ways, and it recommends that such law be reunified through the development of a new uniform act that would subject all charitable gifts to the same set of rules--including a uniform donor-standing rule.

detail.abstract: Previous studies suggest the presence of a "glass cliff" in the sense that women are more likely than men to be appointed to a top leadership position when that position is already risky and precarious. In this study, we examine the theoretical underpinning of the glass cliff hypothesis and empirically test the hypothesis on a large sample of CEO appointments at S&P 1500 firms. A key departure from previous studies is that we characterize precarious CEO positions as those at firms going through a traumatic event or under financial distress. We find no evidence that women are more likely than men to be appointed to such precarious leadership positions. Multivariate probit regression analysis (with controls for firm and CEO characteristics, year and industry fixed effects) further confirms that pre-appointment firm performance and measures for financial distress have no explanatory power for the decision to name a female CEO. The most influential factor is the percentage of women on the board of directors.

detail.abstract: Why do institutions accumulate evidence while repeating failure? This paper introduces a diagnostic framework for identifying anti-learning regimes-institutional configurations in which updating is structurally suppressed despite abundant feedback, expertise, and evaluation. We argue that many apparent failures of adaptation are not informational or behavioural, but architectural: evidence is decoupled from authority, and learning lacks binding force. Building on Institutional Learning Architecture (ILA), we formalise learning suppression as an observable institutional condition and develop measurable indicators of learning fragility, including update suppression rates, feedback penalties, and model rigidity. We identify archetypal anti-learning configurations across public administration, scientific institutions, corporate governance, and policy systems, and distinguish structural learning failure from legitimate disagreement or uncertainty. The framework enables early diagnosis of learning collapse before failures become entrenched, reframing institutional learning not as a cultural attribute but as a governable design property.

detail.abstract: Purpose. This study aimed to test innovative Motivational Interviewing (MI) training strategies: remote workshop and avatar conversation simulations among community mental health staff. Innovation. We provided an engaging, interactive tool for learning and practicing MI to a variety of real-world practitioners and compared two methods for measuring skills: automated scoring from avatar simulations and coded interviews using the validated Motivational Interviewing Treatment Integrity (MITI) tool. Methods. We examined attitudes, beliefs, and MI skills of 127 practitioners implementing three distinct research projects: ACHIEVE-D (weight loss); IMPACT (tobacco smoking cessation); and RHYTHM (CVD risk reduction). Results. 95% of participants believed MI was important to learn; 88% completed the workshop; 64% used the avatar-based training. Practice improvements varied: ACHIEVE-D staff improved in Softening Sustain Talk; IMPACT staff asked fewer questions; RHYTHM staff improved in demonstrating Empathy and Cultivating Change Talk. While underutilized, 47 participants (75%) who tried the avatar training at least once felt that it helped develop their MI skills. Conclusions. Community mental health practitioners value learning MI. Their engagement with the asynchronous avatar training resources was insufficient to significantly impact and sustain their MI skills. Although a novel feature of the avatar-based training, the automated conversation scoring overestimated performance for all MI metrics relative to MITI scores at the same time points.

detail.title: Characterizing Nursing Home Care Team Communication via Text Messaging: A Social Network Analysis
detail.abstract:
Purpose: Communication breakdowns among healthcare teams contribute substantially to preventable adverse events in nursing homes. Although text messaging platforms are increasingly used to support care coordination, little is known about how these technologies are embedded within care team communication networks. The purpose of this study was to characterize patterns of text-message communication among nursing home care teams and to examine how network structures reflect underlying social system dynamics.
Methods: Social network analysis was applied to text messages (n=5,092) linked to (n=585) nursing home-to-hospital resident transfers over 5 years (2015-2020). Message metadata and content were used to construct communication networks and to calculate network measures, including density, centralization (in-degree and out-degree), and reciprocity. Networks were qualitatively classified into communication models based on shared structural characteristics and interpreted using Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovations theory. All analysis and visualization were conducted using Python (3.13.9).
Results: Three distinct communication models were identified. The Integrated model exhibited high message volume, high connectivity, and low hierarchy, consistent with mature adoption of text messaging as a general collaboration tool. The Hub-and-Spoke model showed moderate message volume with centralized information flow, reflecting protocol-driven, hierarchical communication. The Siloed model demonstrated high message volume but low role diversity, indicating niche use within specific professional roles rather than facility-wide coordination. Across models, individuals occupying central or bridging positions appeared to function as informal opinion leaders, influencing communication through frequent interaction rather than formal authority.
Conclusions: The structure and quality of communication networks shape how information flows, influence is exercised through electronic messaging, and innovations are integrated into care processes. Social network analysis offers a rigorous approach for evaluating implementation and guiding strategies to support effective, team-based communication in nursing home settings. Future work should examine whether increasingly integrated communication networks are associated with improved resident outcomes.

title:
Jung, Shadow, and Sex: An Exploration in Psychoanalytic and Poststructuralist Thought

detail.title:
Jung, Shadow, and Sex: An Exploration in Psychoanalytic and Poststructuralist Thought

A Tripartite Psychoanalytic Interrogation: Freud's Id, Jung's Shadow Archetype, and Lacan's Structural Registers in the Dialectics of Repression, Erotic Desire, and Psychic Ontology
detail.abstract:
The shadow, as conceptualized by Carl Gustav Jung, constitutes one of the most primordial and structurally indispensable elements of the human psyche. Unlike the ego, which maintains a precarious coherence through conscious identification, or the persona, which serves as the socially adaptive mask, the shadow encompasses all those aspects of personality that the conscious mind deems unacceptable, inferior, or incompatible with the idealized self-image. Jung describes it as "that hidden, repressed, for the most part inferior and guilt-laden personality" whose ramifications extend into the archaic layers of the collective unconscious, reaching back to our animal ancestors (Jung, 1959/1969, CW 9ii, para. 14). Within this archetypal domain, sexuality emerges not as a peripheral phenomenon but as a central, volatile constituent—intertwined with instinctual life forces, aggressive impulses, and the raw potency of the life instincts themselves.

Jung's divergence from Freud is instructive here. While Freud anchored the unconscious primarily in repressed sexual drives (libido), viewing the psyche through the lens of Oedipal conflict and the pleasure principle, Jung relocated sexuality within a broader archetypal matrix. He acknowledged the sexual instinct as fundamental yet insisted that it participates in a transpersonal, symbolic order that transcends mere biological discharge. In this view, the shadow does not merely contain "repressed" sexual contents in the Freudian sense; rather, it harbors the unacknowledged potency of Eros itself—Eros as both creative union and destructive fusion, capable of manifesting in forms that society and the ego alike experience as threatening. The shadow thus becomes the repository of those sexual energies that threaten the fragile boundaries of civilized identity: polymorphous desires, incestuous fantasies, sadistic and masochistic urges, and the aggressive undercurrents that Freud later theorized as the death drive (Thanatos) but which Jung reframed as an autonomous archetypal force.

detail.abstract: Ethical failures in public-impact institutions often emerge not from individual misconduct but from the design of organizational systems that normalize opacity, discretion, and short-term efficiency at the expense of human dignity. While existing approaches to organizational ethics and humancentered design offer important normative guidance, they are frequently applied instrumentally or retroactively, limiting their preventive capacity. This paper introduces the Human-Centered Ethical Systems Framework (HCESF), a governance-oriented design framework that integrates systems thinking, human-centered ethics, and intergenerational responsibility into institutional architecture. Drawing on applications across internal human resource systems, public service delivery, and healthcare environments, the framework demonstrates how ethical principles can be translated into preventive system design mechanisms such as staged decision-making, transparency, and embedded accountability. By framing institutions as moral stewards responsible for long-term social impact, HCESF provides a transferable model for embedding dignity, fairness, and sustainability into organizational systems with public significance.

detail.title: Predictive Maintenance and Failure Analytics in High-Risk Manufacturing Environments
detail.abstract: This study investigates the integration of predictive maintenance (PdM) and AI-driven failure analytics within high-risk manufacturing environments to enhance operational safety and efficiency. The methodology combines machine learning algorithms with IoT-enabled sensor networks to monitor equipment performance in real time, detect anomalies, and predict potential failures. Environmental risk analytics were incorporated to assess the influence of operational conditions on machinery reliability and to prioritize maintenance interventions. Key findings demonstrate that AI-enabled predictive analytics significantly reduce unplanned downtime, optimize resource allocation, and enhance overall equipment effectiveness. The proactive identification of failure patterns allows maintenance teams to implement timely interventions, thereby mitigating safety hazards and minimizing production disruptions. Furthermore, the approach supports sustainable industrial practices by optimizing energy consumption and extending asset lifecycles. These results highlight the transformative potential of integrating PdM with advanced AI techniques, offering a scalable, data-driven framework for managing complex manufacturing systems. By bridging predictive analytics with operational decision-making, this study provides actionable insights for industries seeking to achieve both safety and sustainability in high-risk production contexts.

detail.title: Critical Analysis of Curriculum Reform Processes: Examining Stakeholder Engagement, Content Appropriateness, and Implementation Frameworks in Primary Education Systems
detail.abstract: Educational curriculum reform represents one of the most consequential and contentious areas of public policy, directly affecting the cognitive, social, moral, and cultural development of future generations. This comprehensive research paper examines the multifaceted dimensions of curriculum reform processes in primary education, with particular attention to the proposed 2026 educational reforms in Sri Lanka. Through systematic analysis of international case studies, established evaluation frameworks, developmental psychology research, and stakeholder engagement models, this study develops a rigorous methodology for assessing curriculum changes. The research emphasizes evidence-based evaluation criteria that balance educational innovation with developmental appropriateness, cultural sensitivity, and democratic participation. By examining successful and unsuccessful reform efforts across multiple national contexts-including the United Kingdom, Sweden, Poland, Singapore, Australia, and Canada-this paper identifies critical success factors and common pitfalls in curriculum development. The findings suggest that curriculum controversies typically arise not solely from content disputes but from inadequate consultation processes, poor communication strategies, insufficient teacher preparation, and failure to address legitimate stakeholder concerns through transparent mechanisms. This research provides actionable recommendations for policymakers, educators, parents, and civil society organizations navigating the complex terrain of educational reform in pluralistic societies.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the integration of Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and probabilistic artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance reliability in industrial systems (Obele, Aikhuele, & Nwosu, 2024). By combining traditional failure analysis techniques with advanced AI-driven probabilistic modeling, the research addresses the limitations of conventional methods in predicting complex system failures. The methodology involved a comprehensive literature synthesis, the design of a hybrid FMEA-RCA-AI framework, and its evaluation through multiple industrial case studies (Gaikwad, 2023). The hybrid framework leverages the systematic identification of potential failure modes, rigorous root cause determination, and probabilistic AI to anticipate failure likelihoods and prioritize mitigation strategies. Key findings demonstrate that the integrated approach significantly improves predictive accuracy, reduces operational failure rates, and strengthens risk mitigation compared to standalone methods (Sabripoor et al., 2024). The results also highlight the adaptability of the framework across diverse industrial contexts, including manufacturing, energy, and process industries. The study concludes that hybrid FMEA-RCA-probabilistic AI frameworks offer superior reliability assessment and proactive risk management, enabling more resilient and efficient industrial operations. These findings provide practical guidance for implementing smart manufacturing strategies and underscore the potential of AI-enhanced reliability analysis to inform decision-making in high-risk industrial environments (Obele et al., 2024; Gaikwad, 2024). Future research should explore longitudinal applications and real-time integration with Industry 4.0 systems to further optimize predictive maintenance and operational safety.

title: Beyond the County Line: Aligning Texas Groundwater Regulation with Reality
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond the County Line: Aligning Texas Groundwater Regulation with Reality
detail.abstract:
Texas groundwater law stands on a precipice. Groundwater is how Texas meets its need for water, but Texas still manages the resource in a mixed system of Groundwater Conservation Districts (GCDs), which are divided by county boundaries but not by the boundaries of the aquifers themselves, meaning that wells that are exactly alike, but on opposite sides of a boundary line, can have different regulations regarding the permitting of these wells merely because they are on different sides of a political line. Some districts require permits to be granted absent clear objections; others place the burden on the landowner and while claiming discretion to request additional information. Others surround each application with automatic contested-case procedures or require costly hydrogeologic studies. The result is a system in which conservation outcomes depend more on local political boundaries than on hydrological reality.

This Comment argues that Texas must bring groundwater regulation in line with the physical reality of its aquifers. Drawing on Chapter 36, the Conservation Amendment, and the Texas Supreme Court’s decisions in Barshop, Day, and Bragg, this Comment explains that the Legislature has adequate constitutional authority to reorganize GCDs along aquifer boundaries without violating the rights of landowners. This Comment proposes that GCDs should be bounded within aquifers similarly to Groundwater Management Areas, identifies alternative funds such as SWIFT, voluntary retirement of water rights, and groundwater easements that would facilitate increased conservation with reduced takings claims, and assesses the special sessions proposals of 2025 to conclude why these bills fail to address the fundamental problem within Texas groundwater law. This Comment outlines a path toward a regulatory system capable of meeting the demands of the future as the state continues to grow.

detail.title: Evaluating Sustainability Metrics in Automated Industrial Production
detail.abstract: The increasing reliance on automated industrial production systems has transformed manufacturing efficiency and scalability, while simultaneously intensifying concerns regarding environmental sustainability, resource consumption, and social responsibility (Ramanujan et al., 2023; Ali et al., 2022). In response to these challenges, this study conducts a structured evaluation of sustainability metrics for automated production environments by integrating advanced automation technologies with artificial intelligence (AI), machine vision, geographic information systems (GIS), and multidimensional environmental performance indicators (Konstantinidis et al., 2021). The study adopts a systematic analytical approach, synthesising evidence from empirical studies, AI-driven sustainability assessment frameworks, and documented industrial case applications to identify prevailing practices and methodological limitations (Ali et al., 2022; Ramanujan et al., 2023). The findings indicate that automation-enabled systems significantly enhance resource efficiency, real-time environmental monitoring, and data accuracy across production processes, thereby supporting more informed sustainability decision-making (Konstantinidis et al., 2021). However, the analysis also reveals persistent gaps in the standardisation, comparability, and holistic integration of sustainability metrics across industries, particularly in linking environmental outcomes with social performance indicators (Ali et al., 2022). The study concludes that the development and adoption of robust, data-driven, and standardised sustainability metrics are critical for effectively aligning automated industrial production with long-term environmental protection and broader social sustainability objectives (Ramanujan et al., 2023).

detail.title: Unequal Climate Policy in an Unequal World
detail.abstract: We characterize optimal climate policy in an economy with heterogeneous households and non-homothetic preferences. We focus on constrained efficiency, where the planner is restricted from transferring resources across households. We derive three results. First, the constrained-optimal carbon tax is heterogeneous and progressive. Second, if restricted to a uniform tax, the optimal rate is lower than the standard Pigouvian level due to inequality. Third, this allocation is decentralizable using only uniform instruments - a carbon tax, clean subsidy, and a lumpsum transfer. In a quantitative application, we show this policy generates a Pareto improvement, reconciling climate efficiency with inequality concerns.

detail.title: Parental Mental Health and the Economic Preferences of the Next Generation
detail.abstract: This paper provides the first evidence that children’s economic preferences vary systematically with parental mental health. Using experimentally elicited measures of economic preferences from more than 4,500 children in Bangladesh, we document that children of parents with indications of mental illness are less prosocial but more patient than their peers with mentally healthy parents. Attitudes toward risk remain unchanged. We discuss potential pathways through which parental mental health may influence the formation of children’s preferences, documenting that children of parents with indication of mental illness assume greater responsibilities within the family, experience less parental involvement, and are exposed to a more adverse home environment.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the identification of entry-order effects in dynamic games of market entry and expansion. When firms are forward-looking and entry timing is strategic, ordinal rank and tenure are endogenously linked through equilibrium behavior, rendering pure entry-order effects generically non-identifiable from reduced-state specifications. I show that commonly estimated rank effects converge to composite objects that mix ordinal position and tenure dynamics, with weights determined by equilibrium entry gaps. I further demonstrate that the conditions required for point identification are fundamentally incompatible with Markov Perfect Equilibrium in most empirically relevant settings.

detail.abstract: This study empirically investigates the causal pathway through which digital showrooms drive sales in the Indian automotive sector. It develops and tests a cohesive model that examines the sequential impact of technology adoption factors on customer experience and, in turn, on sales. To validate the model, a deductive approach was employed, incorporating both descriptive and causal research designs. Using nonprobability convenience sampling, a structured online questionnaire was administered to 251 potential car buyers in India. Hypotheses derived from the theoretical conceptual framework were tested using correlation analysis, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and linear regression. The results supported all the hypotheses (H1-H11). Ease of navigation was identified as the strongest predictor of technology adoption (H3: r = 0.723). Features in digital showrooms, such as interactivity (H4), personalization (H5), AI integration (H6), and convenience (H7), created value for the customer experience. This positive experience led to increased purchase confidence (H8: ρ = 0.692), trust (H9: ρ = 0.636), and likelihood of recommending the showroom to others (H10: ρ = 0.494), directly enhancing sales outcomes. The use of non-probability convenience sampling is considered a primary limitation, as it may affect the generalizability of the results. Future research may employ probability sampling and longitudinal research designs to facilitate cross-cultural comparisons. This study bridges a critical research gap by demonstrating how technology adoption translates into sales through the mediating role of customer experience in the context of automotive digital showrooms.

detail.abstract: Marketers often struggle to convert consumer preferences into commitment. Our research identifies a novel factor—option-presentation order—that marketers can leverage to optimize choice sets and increase consumers’ commitment to their chosen option. Across incentive-compatible studies and real-behavior contexts spanning digital and traditional retail, consumers exhibit stronger commitment to their chosen option when they encounter it at the end of, rather than earlier in, a choice set. This effect is driven by perceived effort payoff—the belief that effort spent searching was worthwhile. As such, the effect is attenuated when the effort payoff experience is constrained, such as when all options are presented simultaneously (vs. sequentially) or when consumers rely on secondhand (vs. firsthand) searches. These findings contribute to research on choice architecture, commitment, and curated choice sets by identifying option-presentation order as a lever for bridging the intention–action gap and designing choice environments that strengthen post-choice commitment.

detail.abstract: This article presents an empirically grounded, interdisciplinary analysis of algorithmic decision-making and the evolving contours of digital due process within Uganda's criminal justice system. Amid increasing adoption of predictive policing tools, AI-powered risk assessments, and automated judicial assistance, this study interrogates how entrenched legal guarantees-such as the right to a fair hearing, the presumption of innocence, and access to legal remedies-are being reshaped by opaque algorithmic logics and data-driven governance. Drawing from 46 semi-structured interviews with judicial officers, prosecutors, police officers, defence attorneys, and detained persons across Kampala, Gulu, and Mbale, and incorporating focus group data and inferential statistical models, the study reveals a critical misalignment between Uganda's constitutional and procedural guarantees and the operational dynamics of imported algorithmic systems. The article synthesises insights from constitutional law, comparative digital rights, socio-technical systems theory, and global south legal epistemologies to critique the technocratic determinism underpinning current deployments. In doing so, it argues for a redesign of fairness standards that moves beyond formal legality and incorporates contextually adaptive algorithmic accountability norms. Key findings include evidence of disproportionate bail denial rates linked to biased risk scores, structural opacity in proprietary predictive tools, and emerging judicial uncertainty regarding the evidentiary admissibility of algorithmic outputs. Proposing a multi-layered normative framework, drawing on jurisprudence from the ECtHR, African Charter mechanisms, and global AI governance initiatives, the paper advances a rights-centred model of digital due process suited to low-resource, high-risk jurisdictions. The analysis contributes to ongoing debates on algorithmic justice, decolonising digital legality, and the operationalization of fairness-by-design in criminal adjudication. It concludes with policy and legislative recommendations, including a draft framework for Uganda's proposed Algorithmic Accountability Bill (2025), offering a replicable prototype for similar jurisdictions in the Global South.

detail.abstract:
Purpose: Brands and trademarks are rather different in essence but complementary phenomena in practice. Trademarks provide legal protection to brands, representing a concrete and measurable asset. They are strategic for brand managers, but they have been relatively neglected in branding studies. This paper aims to delve into an entire trademark registry of a Western economy and identifies the factors that determine trademark duration over the long term.
Design/methodology/approach: To analyze trademark survival, this study relies on the Cox Proportional Hazard Model that estimates the hazard rates as a function of the survival time and a set of covariates. This allows examining the factors influencing the mortality rate of trademarks at a particular point of time through their life span.
Findings: The results reveal that legal oppositions significantly reduce competitors' trademark duration, serving as a protective measure against entrants threatening the market power of incumbents. Also, that the number of assignments/licenses and trademark breadth, reflecting brand value, enhances survival. Finally, other positive factors include the number of trademarks and patents held by applicants, as well as their status as nonresidents or firms.
Originality/value-The investigation analyzes all existing trademarks recorded in the first official registry of the world-institutionalized in Spain in 1850-and tracks their longevity up to 2010. This is an original approach that contributes to the understanding of the long-term consequences of distinct legal, commercial and administrative trademark strategies. The results provide interesting insights for both branding scholars and practitioners.

detail.abstract: The integration of predictive algorithms into clinical practice represents a significant transformation. Deployed as clinical decision support tools, these algorithms promise greater precision and efficiency in decision-making. However, concerns persist that they may absorb, codify, or even amplify historical biases in care delivery. We examine this trade-off by quantifying the downstream consequences of hospitals' algorithm adoption. Using a difference-indifferences analysis of 308,137 inpatient admissions for acute coronary syndrome, we find that algorithm adoption alters care resource allocation: high-severity patients are more likely to receive diagnostic testing and intensive treatments, whereas care for low-severity patients is de-escalated. These shifts translate into a significant reduction in in-hospital mortality for high-severity patients, while outcomes for low-severity patients remain unchanged. The survival benefits, however, are not equitably shared. Within the high-severity group, the mortality reduction accrues exclusively to White patients, whereas non-White patients experience no significant improvement. Consistent with this disparity, non-White patients are less likely than White patients to receive diagnostic testing and intensive treatments following adoption. Our study provides large-scale evidence that technologies designed for efficiency can deepen health inequities, underscoring the need to manage algorithmic tools for equitable outcomes.

title: Measuring the Space Economy with Input-Output Linkages

detail.title: Measuring the Space Economy with Input-Output Linkages
detail.abstract: Space-enabled technologies underpin communications, navigation, Earth observation, and critical infrastructure, but widely cited estimates of the space economy often rely on proprietary classifications or revenue tallies that abstract from production linkages. We develop a transparent, national-accounts framework to measure the U.S. footprint of a conservative set of core space industries using input-output total requirements tables with real gross output and value added by industry. The framework decomposes activity into direct core output and indirect spillovers through upstream suppliers and downstream users, and it produces measures of exposure and supplier concentration. Indirect activity exceeds direct activity in every benchmark year and grows faster over time: direct core output rises from just under $60B in 2007 to $75-80B by 2017, while the associated indirect component increases from about $80-85B to roughly $120-125B, implying an indirect to direct ratio near 1.6 by 2017. In projections to 2030 using an input-output consistent protocol with scenario wedges and Monte Carlo uncertainty bands, the baseline total footprint reaches about $350B.

title: Quad-O’s Effect on International Crude Oil, Distillate Prices, and Industry Returns
affiliations: University of Texas of the Permian Basin

detail.title: Quad-O’s Effect on International Crude Oil, Distillate Prices, and Industry Returns
detail.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency’s Quad-O regulation’s objective is to reduce methane emissions; however, its effects on industry output and international crude oil and natural gas prices remain poorly understood. Quad-O increased international prices for crude oil, natural gas, conventional gas, diesel, and aviation fuel, but did not produce uniform effects on firm returns across upstream, midstream, and downstream sectors. While the regulation’s implementation had limited effects on most firm returns, equipment & services and transportation & pipeline sectors experienced adverse returns following the Quad-O announcement. Although consumers faced higher energy prices, these sectoral return differential effects suggest that oil and gas consumers bore a larger share of the regulatory burden.

title: Learning by AI: Market Intelligence and Exporting
affiliations: Georgetown University School of Foreign Service in Qatar, , Peking University - School of Economics and Peking University - School of Economics

detail.title: Learning by AI: Market Intelligence and Exporting
detail.abstract: Early adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) reshaped how firms responded to market dynamics by enhancing data collection and analysis. Linking China's universe of customs shipments to millions of online job ads, we tracked AI hiring in sales, marketing, and analytics to build a firm-level proxy for non-production AI and map its exposure across products within firms. To structure our analysis, we introduce a model in which firms confront asymmetric information about heterogeneous consumer preferences and show that AI mitigates these frictions by sharpening firms' ability to learn demand patterns across markets. The model predicts — and the data confirm — that AI-intensive firms fine-tune their product mix and prices with greater precision: they are more likely to export, expand their product lines, and adjust market choices. Crucially, this refinement appears as narrower price dispersion but wider quantity dispersion across destinations — effects strongest for differentiated goods, larger firms, and sales to high-income economies. Together, the evidence shows that AI eases demand-side information frictions, allowing firms to optimize their global reach strategies.
